dataset_description: Monthly distinct customer counts (April-June 2026) per dealer, with a trend label based on month-over-month decline, for a fixed 10-dealer sample.

reporting_period_logic.customer_count_definition: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_code) per dealer per month
reporting_period_logic.missing_month_handling: For dealers with activity in at least one selected month, missing months default to 0.

customer_count_apr_may_jun.description: April, May, and June distinct customer counts joined as a single comma-separated text string.

customer_count_trend.description: Trend label: 'Declining: X%' if at least 2 of the 3 month-over-month comparisons (Apr vs Mar, May vs Apr, Jun vs May) show a decline, otherwise 'Stable'.
customer_count_trend.declining_rule: at least 2 of the 3 month-over-month checks show a drop
customer_count_trend.declining_value: 'Declining: ' followed by the average of the declining months' percentage drop, rounded to 2 decimals, followed by '%'
customer_count_trend.stable_value: 'Stable' (used whenever fewer than 2 of the 3 months show a decline)

llm_instructions: customer_count_trend is only labelled 'Declining' when at least 2 of the 3 month-over-month checks (Apr vs Mar, May vs Apr, Jun vs May) show a drop; otherwise it is 'Stable'.
Do not describe a 'Stable' label as meaning the customer counts were flat or unchanged — check customer_count_apr_may_jun for the actual monthly values before describing the pattern.
Support any statement with the actual values in customer_count_apr_may_jun.
Do not invent reasons (e.g. seasonality, lost customers, competitor activity) for a decline or stability.
customer_count_apr_may_jun only contains April, May, and June values; March is used internally for the April comparison but is not shown in the output.
Parse the comma-separated string to extract individual monthly counts before generating narrative.
